newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia Yield Spreads-Stay under pressure.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia Yield Spreads-Stay under pressure.

text.p: Australian bonds continued to severely underperform against the U.S. and Canada as data continued to show an improving economy, although analysts believe that the widening in differentials has been overdone.
The local market came under intense pressure again today after retail trade rebounded 2.7 percent in January and building approvals jumped 10.4 percent, way above market expectations.
"Signs of accelerating demand is clearly bearish for interest rate markets," said economists at Citibank Australia.

"But for the longer end of the curve, the propect of low price deflators in (Wednesday's) National Accounts, the low inflation readings in the Q1 CPI release, and a market friendly Budget in May suggest that at 130 basis points over the U.S., 10-year yield are oversold in the shorterm," they added.
Citibank see a retest of 7.50 percent on the 10-year yield and sub 100 basis points on the spread to U.S. as reasonable short term targets.
Local fourth quarter GDP is due at 11.30 a.m. (0030 GMT) on Wednesday.

This spread comes despite the continued heavy tone of U.S. Treasuries ahead of Wednesday's second leg of Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony, and Friday key non-farm payrolls report for February.
This is also weighing on Canadian debt.
Meanwhile, New Zealand bonds were dragged back by the weakness of the Australian debt market and after N.Z. Treasurer Winston Peters delivered few surprises in the Budget Policy Statement.
